articles.title: Expert analysis: Three key takeaways from latest China-EU trade talks
articles.titleCn: 专家分析：中欧最新贸易谈判的三大关键要点
articles.summary: CGTN takes a deeper look at the latest joint statement that addresses China-EU economic and trade ties.
articles.summaryCn: 中欧联合声明在电动汽车出口、医疗器械进口、稀土出口和知识产权等关键议题上达成16项协议，专家认为这体现了双方合作意愿、中国致力于更平衡的贸易关系，以及中国是解决欧洲问题的伙伴而非根源。

paragraphs.en:
China and the European Union (EU) released a joint statement on Friday {{0}} a list of 16 agreements, including a reduction in China's electric vehicle exports, increased imports of European medical devices and {{1}} concerning rare earth exports and intellectual property management – all key issues at the center of trade tensions between the two sides. After a {{2}} period of {{3}} China-EU trade tensions, the joint statement offered a much-needed easing of tensions, bringing both sides back to dialogue and {{4}} enhanced cooperation and mutual understanding. To unpack the joint statement and examine the significance of the {{5}}, CGTN spoke to Jiang Feng, a research professor at the Shanghai Academy of Global Governance and Area Studies (SAGGAS), dean of the Institute for European Studies and chairman of the SAGGAS Council, who shared three key takeaways from the statement. Takeaway 1: Both sides demonstrate strong {{6}} to cooperate and engage in dialogue
Jiang said the joint statement marked an initial success and sent a clear signal: both sides had demonstrated a strong willingness to cooperate and wanted to avoid a trade war. Words such as "dialogue," "communication" and "cooperation" appear repeatedly in the joint statement, highlighting both sides' willingness to engage with each other in a mutually beneficial manner.
paragraphs.cn: 中国和欧盟周五发布联合声明，列出了一系列共16项协议，包括减少中国电动汽车出口、增加欧洲医疗器械进口，以及有关稀土出口和知识产权管理的承诺——这些都是双方贸易紧张关系的核心关键议题。在经历了长期酝酿的中欧贸易紧张局势之后，这份联合声明带来了亟需的紧张局势缓和，使双方重回对话轨道，并释放出加强合作与相互理解的信号。为解读这份联合声明并审视此次磋商的意义，CGTN采访了上海全球治理与区域国别研究院（SAGGAS）研究教授、欧洲研究所所长兼SAGGAS理事会主席姜锋，他分享了这份声明的三大关键要点。要点一：双方展现出强烈的合作与对话意愿。姜锋表示，这份联合声明标志着初步成功，并释放出明确信号：双方都展现出强烈的合作意愿，希望避免贸易战。“对话”“沟通”和“合作”等词语在联合声明中反复出现，凸显了双方以互利方式开展交往的意愿。

paragraphs.en: Jiang noted that while both sides have made compromises, the agreements between China and the EU were based on {{7}} and equality. "While addressing the EU's concerns, China has also raised its own demands, including fair treatment and a favorable business environment for Chinese enterprises operating in Europe, urging the EU to refrain from adopting {{8}} measures against Chinese companies in areas such as public {{9}}," he noted. Beyond a step that stabilizes China-EU relations, Jiang also pointed out that {{10}} consultations carry significance in the greater global context. "Now that the two sides can sit down and negotiate a resolution to the pressing – and indeed serious – economic and trade issues they face, this not only serves the interests of China and Europe but also sets a good example for countries around the world to resolve {{11}} disputes and differences through consultation," Jiang said. In other words, success in reaching {{12}} between China and the EU on trade differences through a dialogue mechanism is not just an achievement for both sides but also a win for global economic stability and a rules-based trade order.
paragraphs.cn: 姜锋指出，尽管双方都作出了妥协，但中欧之间的协议建立在互惠和平等的基础之上。他指出：“在回应欧方关切的同时，中国也提出了自身诉求，包括为在欧洲经营的中国企业争取公平待遇和有利的营商环境，敦促欧盟避免在公共采购等领域对中国企业采取歧视性措施。”除了稳定中欧关系之外，姜锋还指出，建设性磋商在更广泛的全球背景下也具有重要意义。姜锋说：“既然双方能够坐下来协商解决他们所面临的紧迫——而且确实严峻的——经贸问题，这不仅符合中欧双方的利益，也为世界各国通过协商解决双边争端和分歧树立了良好榜样。”换言之，中欧通过对话机制在贸易分歧上达成共识，不仅是双方的成就，也是全球经济稳定和基于规则的贸易秩序的胜利。

paragraphs.en:
Takeaway 2: China is committed to working toward a more balanced trade relationship with the EU
Jiang noted that as a result of the consultations, the EU had secured demands it urgently sought, while China had honored its commitments and addressed major EU concerns. China has agreed to reduce its exports of new energy vehicles, increase imports of EU medical devices, lower tariffs and address existing market access barriers, reflecting its commitment to more balanced trade relations. The first major demand comes from Europe's automobile industry, "a key sector for Europe and the area where the EU feels the greatest pressure from China," according to Jiang. He said that the consensus to control the total volume of Chinese automobile exports to Europe is highly {{13}} and responds to the biggest demand of the automobile industries in Germany and other European countries. The second area of concern involves tariffs and rare earth export licensing, where room for adjustment has opened up.
paragraphs.cn: 要点二：中国致力于推动与欧盟建立更加平衡的贸易关系。姜锋指出，经过磋商，欧盟获得了其迫切寻求的诉求，而中国也履行了承诺并回应了欧盟的主要关切。中国已同意减少新能源汽车出口、增加欧盟医疗器械进口、降低关税并解决现有的市场准入壁垒，体现了其推动更平衡贸易关系的承诺。据姜锋介绍，第一大诉求来自欧洲汽车产业，“这是欧洲的关键产业，也是欧盟感受到来自中国最大压力的领域”。他表示，控制中国对欧洲汽车出口总量的共识具有高度实质性，回应了德国及其他欧洲国家汽车产业的最大诉求。第二个关切领域涉及关税和稀土出口许可，在这方面已经打开了调整空间。

paragraphs.en:
According to Jiang, the fast-track mechanism {{14}} export licenses for rare earths and permanent magnets supplied to the EU is extremely important for the EU, who had previously expressed an urgent need for progress in this area. What China demonstrated in the dialogue has been consistent with what it has long claimed: that China is willing to maintain stable bilateral economic and trade ties and make them more balanced with the EU. Takeaway 3: China is not the root cause of Europe's problems but a partner in solving them
Wang Wentao, the Chinese minister of commerce who represented China in the consultations, has said that "China is not the source of Europe's problems but a partner in solving them." The message is clear here: trade cooperation between China and the EU will benefit rather than harm both sides. In recent years, however, {{15}} of China as an economic threat have continued to grow in some European countries, referencing a huge trade deficit of €360 billion. Jiang warned against such characterizations, calling for closer {{16}} of the figures used to support these narratives and cautioning against the {{17}} of portraying China as a threat.
paragraphs.cn: 据姜锋介绍，为供应欧盟的稀土和永磁体提供出口许可便利的快速通道机制对欧盟极为重要，欧盟此前曾表示迫切需要在这一领域取得进展。中国在对话中展现的立场与其长期主张一致：中国愿意维持稳定的双边经贸关系，并使其与欧盟之间更加平衡。要点三：中国不是欧洲问题的根源，而是解决问题的伙伴。代表中国参加磋商的中国商务部部长王文涛曾表示：“中国不是欧洲问题的根源，而是解决问题的伙伴。”这里传递的信息很明确：中欧贸易合作将惠及而非损害双方。然而近年来，一些欧洲国家将中国视为经济威胁的看法持续升温，并援引高达3600亿欧元的巨额贸易逆差。姜锋对此类定性提出警告，呼吁更仔细地审视用于支撑这些叙事的数字，并告诫将中国描绘为威胁可能带来的后果。

paragraphs.en:
While the EU has repeatedly highlighted a trade deficit with China of more than €1 billion ($1.12 billion) per day, Jiang noted that this figure also counted in the substantial volume of goods produced by European companies in China and then sold back to Europe, which are in fact European companies selling to Europe. Additionally, Jiang noted that the {{18}} figure is the EU's goods trade deficit with China and does not account for its substantial {{19}} of trade in services with China, which leads to a {{20}} of the overall economic and trade relationship. Not only does the evidence underpinning the "China threat" narrative appear shaky, the result of spreading the political narrative of China as the cause of Europe's problems can also be damaging. "Presenting {{21}} as damage to European {{22}} and security is a classic case of extreme politicization and securitization of economic and trade issues," Jiang warned. "It will push up trade costs, tear apart industrial chains, {{23}} bilateral trust and ultimately harm the economic well-being of all parties."
Cooperation may, however, bring a very different future.
paragraphs.cn: 尽管欧盟多次强调对华贸易逆差每天超过10亿欧元（11.2亿美元），姜锋指出，这一数字也计入了欧洲公司在中国生产然后回销欧洲的大量商品，而这些实际上是欧洲公司在向欧洲销售。此外，姜锋指出，这个惊人的数字是欧盟对华货物贸易逆差，并未计入其在服务贸易中对中国的巨额顺差，这导致对整体经贸关系的误读。不仅支撑“中国威胁”叙事的证据显得站不住脚，散布中国是欧洲问题根源这一政治叙事的后果也可能具有破坏性。姜锋警告说：“将相互依存描绘为对欧洲主权和安全的损害，是经贸问题极端政治化和安全化的典型案例。这将推高贸易成本、撕裂产业链、侵蚀双边互信，最终损害各方的经济福祉。”然而，合作可能带来截然不同的未来。

paragraphs.en: Jiang suggests that China and the EU are both export-oriented economies that have the potential not only to strengthen each other but also to jointly contribute to a more stable global trade order. Jiang observed that in the joint statement, many of the agreements in the China-EU joint statement are framed within the broader context of the World Trade Organization (WTO). In other words, both sides are deliberately working together to build confidence in and {{24}} the authority of the WTO's fair-trade principles, which implies a potential for China-EU cooperation to strengthen {{25}} of the global trading order. "I believe it is important to translate the valuable experience and the approaches used to resolve problems between China and the EU into principles that can promote the governance of the global trading system," Jiang said.
paragraphs.cn: 姜锋认为，中国和欧盟都是出口导向型经济体，不仅有能力相互成就，也有能力共同为更加稳定的全球贸易秩序作出贡献。姜锋观察到，在中欧联合声明中，许多协议都置于世界贸易组织（WTO）的更广泛框架之内。换言之，双方正在有意携手，为WTO公平贸易原则树立信心并维护其权威，这意味着中欧合作有潜力加强全球贸易秩序的治理。姜锋说：“我认为，重要的是将中欧之间解决分歧的宝贵经验和做法转化为能够促进全球贸易体系治理的原则。”

articles.fullText:
China and the European Union (EU) released a joint statement on Friday outlining a list of 16 agreements, including a reduction in China's electric vehicle exports, increased imports of European medical devices and commitments concerning rare earth exports and intellectual property management – all key issues at the center of trade tensions between the two sides.
After a prolonged period of simmering China-EU trade tensions, the joint statement offered a much-needed easing of tensions, bringing both sides back to dialogue and signaling enhanced cooperation and mutual understanding.
To unpack the joint statement and examine the significance of the consultations, CGTN spoke to Jiang Feng, a research professor at the Shanghai Academy of Global Governance and Area Studies (SAGGAS), dean of the Institute for European Studies and chairman of the SAGGAS Council, who shared three key takeaways from the statement.
Takeaway 1: Both sides demonstrate strong willingness to cooperate and engage in dialogue
Jiang said the joint statement marked an initial success and sent a clear signal: both sides had demonstrated a strong willingness to cooperate and wanted to avoid a trade war.
Words such as "dialogue," "communication" and "cooperation" appear repeatedly in the joint statement, highlighting both sides' willingness to engage with each other in a mutually beneficial manner.
Jiang noted that while both sides have made compromises, the agreements between China and the EU were based on reciprocity and equality.
"While addressing the EU's concerns, China has also raised its own demands, including fair treatment and a favorable business environment for Chinese enterprises operating in Europe, urging the EU to refrain from adopting discriminatory measures against Chinese companies in areas such as public procurement," he noted.
Beyond a step that stabilizes China-EU relations, Jiang also pointed out that constructive consultations carry significance in the greater global context.
"Now that the two sides can sit down and negotiate a resolution to the pressing – and indeed serious – economic and trade issues they face, this not only serves the interests of China and Europe but also sets a good example for countries around the world to resolve bilateral disputes and differences through consultation," Jiang said.
In other words, success in reaching consensus between China and the EU on trade differences through a dialogue mechanism is not just an achievement for both sides but also a win for global economic stability and a rules-based trade order.
Takeaway 2: China is committed to working toward a more balanced trade relationship with the EU
Jiang noted that as a result of the consultations, the EU had secured demands it urgently sought, while China had honored its commitments and addressed major EU concerns.
China has agreed to reduce its exports of new energy vehicles, increase imports of EU medical devices, lower tariffs and address existing market access barriers, reflecting its commitment to more balanced trade relations.
The first major demand comes from Europe's automobile industry, "a key sector for Europe and the area where the EU feels the greatest pressure from China," according to Jiang.
He said that the consensus to control the total volume of Chinese automobile exports to Europe is highly substantive and responds to the biggest demand of the automobile industries in Germany and other European countries.
The second area of concern involves tariffs and rare earth export licensing, where room for adjustment has opened up. According to Jiang, the fast-track mechanism facilitating export licenses for rare earths and permanent magnets supplied to the EU is extremely important for the EU, who had previously expressed an urgent need for progress in this area.
What China demonstrated in the dialogue has been consistent with what it has long claimed: that China is willing to maintain stable bilateral economic and trade ties and make them more balanced with the EU.
Takeaway 3: China is not the root cause of Europe's problems but a partner in solving them
Wang Wentao, the Chinese minister of commerce who represented China in the consultations, has said that "China is not the source of Europe's problems but a partner in solving them." The message is clear here: trade cooperation between China and the EU will benefit rather than harm both sides.
In recent years, however, perceptions of China as an economic threat have continued to grow in some European countries, referencing a huge trade deficit of €360 billion.
Jiang warned against such characterizations, calling for closer scrutiny of the figures used to support these narratives and cautioning against the ramifications of portraying China as a threat.
While the EU has repeatedly highlighted a trade deficit with China of more than €1 billion ($1.12 billion) per day, Jiang noted that this figure also counted in the substantial volume of goods produced by European companies in China and then sold back to Europe, which are in fact European companies selling to Europe.
Additionally, Jiang noted that the staggering figure is the EU's goods trade deficit with China and does not account for its substantial surplus of trade in services with China, which leads to a misrepresentation of the overall economic and trade relationship.
Not only does the evidence underpinning the "China threat" narrative appear shaky, the result of spreading the political narrative of China as the cause of Europe's problems can also be damaging.
"Presenting interdependence as damage to European sovereignty and security is a classic case of extreme politicization and securitization of economic and trade issues," Jiang warned. "It will push up trade costs, tear apart industrial chains, erode bilateral trust and ultimately harm the economic well-being of all parties."
Cooperation may, however, bring a very different future. Jiang suggests that China and the EU are both export-oriented economies that have the potential not only to strengthen each other but also to jointly contribute to a more stable global trade order.
Jiang observed that in the joint statement, many of the agreements in the China-EU joint statement are framed within the broader context of the World Trade Organization (WTO). In other words, both sides are deliberately working together to build confidence in and uphold the authority of the WTO's fair-trade principles, which implies a potential for China-EU cooperation to strengthen governance of the global trading order.
"I believe it is important to translate the valuable experience and the approaches used to resolve problems between China and the EU into principles that can promote the governance of the global trading system," Jiang said.

articles.title: China unveils five-year plan for new-type battery industry
articles.titleCn: 中国发布新型电池产业五年规划
articles.summary: China has issued a development plan for its new-type battery industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), setting targets for industrial growth, technological innovation and product quality.
articles.summaryCn: 中国多部门联合发布新型电池产业发展规划，提出到2030年在先进材料、新型电池体系、全固态电池规模化应用等方面取得突破，并设定产业增长、技术创新和产品质量目标。

articles.fullText:
The displayed solid-state battery and hydrogen power technologies in China's FAW Museum in Changchun, Jilin Province, August 1, 2026. 
China has issued a development plan for its new-type battery industry during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), setting targets for industrial growth, technological innovation and product quality.
The plan, jointly issued by multiple government departments including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), aims for steady industry growth and stronger innovation capabilities across the entire industrial chain by 2030.
By 2030, China aims to achieve breakthroughs in advanced electrode materials, new electrolytes and high-end auxiliary materials, and make major progress in the development of new battery systems.
The plan envisions the initial large-scale application of all-solid-state batteries and a cycle life of 15,000 cycles for long-life lithium batteries by 2030.
Product defect rates at leading enterprises are expected to reach the parts-per-billion level by 2030, according to the plan.
New-type batteries are high-efficiency devices or systems for storing and converting electrical energy, including lithium, sodium and flow batteries, with innovation focused on new operating principles, materials, structures and manufacturing processes.
In China, electric vehicles, the low-altitude economy, consumer electronics and humanoid robotics are generating demand for high-performance batteries, while battery-based energy storage is being used to support renewable energy integration and improve power grid stability.
China's new-type battery industry saw its output value exceed 1 trillion yuan (about $149 billion) during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025), according to the MIIT.
This is China's first dedicated national-level plan for the battery industry, said Nan Cewen, a professor at Tsinghua University and an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Nan said that the plan builds on the country's industrial scale and supply-chain strengths to guide the industry's future development.
It outlines 19 priority tasks across five areas, including innovation throughout the industrial chain, industrial upgrading and development of the industrial system.
Key measures include accelerating technological breakthroughs needed for the industrial-scale production of all-solid-state batteries and developing a product supply system centered on lithium batteries, complemented by sodium and flow batteries.
Other measures include improving the safety and all-climate performance of power batteries for new energy vehicles, accelerating the development of standards for key technologies shared across the industry and advanced technologies suited to practical use, strengthening intellectual property protection and improving battery life-cycle traceability.
The plan calls for faster integration and innovation involving new-type battery technologies, clean energy and end-use applications, as well as closer integration of international trade and investment in the industry.

articles.fullText:
September 29 marks the International Day of Awareness of Food Loss and Waste. According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), an estimated 13.2% of food produced globally, equivalent to 1.25 billion tonnes, is lost after harvest and before reaching retail.
As food travels from fields to tables, it passes through multiple stages including planting, harvesting, storage, transportation and processing. Reducing losses at each stage has become a critical component of safeguarding food security. In recent years, the accelerated application of smart agriculture, intelligent machinery, green grain storage and digital monitoring technologies has provided strong support for ensuring that every grain makes it to the granary.
In the field harvest stage, intelligent agricultural machinery is transforming traditional practices. According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, China's wheat, rice and corn mechanized harvest loss rates in 2024 were 0.93%, 1.76% and 2.06%, respectively, representing a reduction of 1 to 2 percentage points compared with 2021. Over three years, more than 25 million tonnes of grain losses were reduced. In east China's Shandong Province, the average mechanized wheat harvest loss rate reached 0.81% in 2024.
According to data released by the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration in October 2025, based on surveys over the past three years, the comprehensive loss rate during grain storage periods in grain depots is kept below 1%, with losses mainly consisting of natural reductions as a result of moisture and impurities. The administration launched its first batch of 30 demonstration sites for integrated green grain storage technologies in 2025, with the "five-in-one" technology system gradually being refined.
Regarding broader grain circulation, Qin Yuyun, deputy director of the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, stated at a press conference held by the State Council Information Office on October 14, 2025, that in recent years, the average annual grain loss during storage, processing and transportation accounted for approximately 2% of total annual grain production. The loss rate during grain transportation has been reduced to 0.8 per thousand.
The Action Plan for Food Saving and Anti-Food Waste, issued by the General Offices of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the State Council on November 25, 2024, sets clear targets: by the end of 2027, grain loss rates in production, storage, transportation and processing should be controlled below the international average level. As agricultural science and technology continue to penetrate the entire industrial chain, the concept that “reducing loss is increasing grain” is being translated into tangible results.

The African Union's panel of facilitators has called for strict adherence to ceasefire commitments and continued diplomatic engagement to end fighting in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, following consultations in the M23-held city of Goma.
The panel said on Wednesday that lasting peace would require political dialogue and urged the parties to engage in good faith in the Doha peace process, while cooperating fully with ceasefire monitoring mechanisms.
A delegation led by Sahle-Work Zewde, former president of Ethiopia and deputy chairperson of the panel, held talks in Goma earlier this week with representatives of the United Nations peacekeeping mission in Congo, known as MONUSCO, UN and humanitarian agencies, as well as the M23 rebel group, the AU said.
Former Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta and former Botswanan President Mokgweetsi Masisi were also part of the delegation.
"Lasting peace requires political dialogue," the panel said, calling for restraint and warning against actions that could undermine the peace process.
Qatar has mediated talks between the Congolese government and M23 since March 2025. The negotiations have produced a declaration of principles and a framework agreement, with both sides committing to build trust through dialogue, advance stabilization in stages and address the underlying causes of the conflict.
The AU panel also called for greater protection of civilians and safe, unhindered humanitarian access. It said the findings from its consultations would be shared with the AU mediator and the Congolese government, while engagement would continue to build confidence and advance negotiations.
Corneille Nangaa, leader of the Congo River Alliance, a politico-military coalition allied with M23, told reporters in Goma on Wednesday that mediators should "go beyond general statements."
Nangaa called for "precise, clear and verifiable commitments" backed by mechanisms to monitor their implementation. He said the Doha process would only be sustainable if it addressed the root causes of the conflict and produced concrete measures to protect civilians.
Since January 2025, the M23 rebel group has intensified offensives in the eastern provinces of North Kivu and South Kivu, seizing several key cities, including Goma and Bukavu.

President Donald Trump speaks while meeting with Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham during the United Nations General Assembly, at the UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 22, 2026. 
US President Donald Trump on Monday said that a Minnesota company plans to build a multi-billion-dollar steel mill in Iowa, handing the administration a marquee manufacturing investment to showcase as Republicans head into November's midterm elections.
Trump unveiled the project at the White House with executives from Mesabi Metallics, which recently opened Minnesota's first new iron ore mine in 50 years. The White House said the plant investment would amount to $15 billion.
The announcement comes as Trump seeks to bolster his economic record ahead of November's election, with his approval rating plumbing all-time lows of late as the Republican Party confronts voter concerns about inflation and the cost of living. Trump has made tariffs and a revival of US manufacturing central to his economic agenda, arguing that higher barriers to imports will drive investment and jobs back to the United States.
But Republicans are in the midst of several competitive elections in Iowa, a once-swingy state that has more consistently voted for Trump's party in recent years. Polling this cycle shows a tight race for a seat in the US Senate, as well as its gubernatorial race, where the Democratic candidate, Rob Sand, has led most polls.
The potential $15 billion steel project gives Trump a high-profile investment to tout as he makes that case to voters. It also comes as the administration faces pressure to show that its policies imposing broad tariffs on US imports can deliver industrial gains without fueling inflation.
"This is a tremendous investment," Trump said in the White House's Oval Office. "Our steel industry is roaring back to life."
